notes: vanguardngr.com: 693 unique article URLs, 31/31 days in window; per-day counts 21-23 (2026-09-30=22, 2026-10-10=23, 2026-10-20=23), 34 polite_fetch requests, ~22 s. ROUTE: the site's own per-day WordPress date archives https://www.vanguardngr.com/YYYY/MM/DD/ (page 1 only). Each archive renders <article> cards holding the post URL (/YYYY/MM/slug/) plus the site's own per-post date text ('October 10, 2026'), so the listed date is the site's, not inferred; the card date is used, and the archive day only as fallback. robots.txt (status 200): Crawl-delay 10 and 30, Disallow /wp-json/, /search/, /*s=*/, /wp-admin/, /cgi-bin/, /xmlrpc.php; only /feed/ explicitly allowed. CLOSED ROUTES: /wp-json/wp/v2/posts (robots-disallowed); every sitemap from robots.txt and variants - /sitemap_index.xml 403, /news-sitemap.xml 403, /sitemap.xml 403, /post-sitemap.xml 403, non-www host 403, query-busted 403 (so the usual WP-REST or sitemap-lastmod routes were unavailable); archive pagination /2026/10/10/page/2/ 403, /page/2 403, ?paged=2 403 (WAF), so only page 1 of each day is reachable - that is why each day gives ~22 of the outlet's ~200 daily posts, which is still well above the 15/day bar; /feed/ is 200 but 20 items per page (~2 h of publication at ~200 posts/day), so reaching back 31 days would need ~370 requests and was rejected. VERIFIED: 4 articles re-fetched (one per target day plus a random one) all HTTP 200, 3191-6911 chars of body text, and JSON-LD datePublished == article:published_time == the listed date exactly (e.g. 2026-10-10T18:30:18+00:00). Script prints per-day counts, has a 15-minute internal deadline, retries a failed day once, dedupes by URL and writes URL<TAB>YYYY-MM-DD with no header.
